title: Summary: built a browser WASD teleop stack for a four-node NXP distributed-ECU car (MCXA153 + 2 Arduinos + ESP32), moved the sonars to front/back, then debugged it down through a hung I2C wait, a GPIO1 held in reset, and a floating I2C bus with no pull-ups

parts: You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude, assisting with software engineering tasks in the user's NXP Summer School distributed-ECU vehicle project.

lets make a prototype script for my project. i connected all the components from the schema. make me a site from where i can control the car using "WASD" (S will be braking only, as we dont have reverse). on the same page, i want to be able to send messages to the display to be viewed and also i want to be able to see live data from all sensors. also change the schema for D3 D7 HC-SR04P as the front sensor and the other one as the back sensor. I want to use SPACE to horn. keep in mind that frdm mcxa 153 is the brain! it needs to take my input through esp32 and send signals to the arduinos

The prototype is built and everything that can be compiled here, compiles.

## What it does

Browser -> ESP32 -> I2C -> MCXA153 -> UART -> PERC/ACT. The page sends key state only: K,<w>,<a>,<s>,<d>,<horn> at 10 Hz plus on every change. The throttle ramp, steering mix, duty cap, obstacle veto and watchdogs all live on the MCX, so a bad or lagging browser can only stop sending keys.

- W ramps throttle (0->65% in ~1.1 s), A/D take 28 points off that side, S brakes to zero. At standstill A/D pivot instead - one side driven, other held off, since there's no reverse.
- SPACE -> VCU sends H,1 to PERC at 4 Hz. PERC kills the buzzer 500 ms after the last one, so a lost "off" can't leave it sounding.
- Message box -> M,<text> -> ACT's 1602A row 0, marqueeing past 16 chars; row 1 stays live drive state.
- Live data: front/back ranges, PIR, motor duties, throttle, horn, guard, MPU6050, plus per-node link ages so a dead Arduino is visible from the browser.

Three timeouts in series: browser stops on blur/close -> VCU releases after 400 ms -> ACT cuts motors after 300 ms.

## Sonar change

D3/D7 is now front, D2/D6 is back - in SCHEMA_WIRING.svg, SCHEMA_SIGNALS.svg, FULL_SCHEMA.md, perc.ino and test_perc.ino. Front vetoes forward throttle under 25 cm while still allowing a pivot; back is a readout only, since there's no reverse for it to protect. Ranging is now interrupt-driven on INT0/INT1 rather than pulseIn().

Two things worth flagging:

- The splayed left/right pair is gone, and with it the left/right range comparison the schema's autonomy argument was built on. Right call for a driven car, but if autonomy comes back you need the splayed pair or a third sensor. I wrote this into section 5 rather than quietly dropping it.
- I fixed a transport bug in link.c: link_gw_poll fetched a fresh I2C chunk per line and discarded everything after the first newline. At 48 bytes a chunk that's ~3 of every 4 key updates dropped. It now holds the chunk between calls.

## Verified

- VCU firmware builds clean, no warnings under -Wall -Wextra (28% flash, 20% RAM)
- perc.ino, act.ino, test_perc.ino compile for Uno (22/26/15% flash)
- Page JS parses; I rendered it against a mock gateway and confirmed keypad highlighting, bars, and the BLOCKED state

Done - the ESP32 now joins Redmi Note 12 Pro 5G. Both sketches rebuilt clean.

Two things I added that you didn't ask for, because they'd have bitten you:

1. WiFi.setSleep(false) - this is the one that matters. In station mode the ESP32 defaults to modem sleep and wakes on the phone's beacon, roughly every 100 ms. A packet arriving just after a wake waits for the next one, so you'd get up to 100 ms added to every keypress, on a control path budgeted at 20 ms. The car would feel broken, not laggy, and nothing in the code would look wrong. AP mode never sleeps, which is why this wasn't a problem before.

2. AP fallback. If the hotspot isn't found in 15 s, it brings up NXP-AV / distributed at 192.168.4.1 and carries on. Your schema chose AP mode deliberately so no network you don't control can kill the demo; a phone is yours, but it can be off, flat, or taking a call.

The address is no longer fixed - the Serial Monitor prints it, http://nxpav.local also works via mDNS, and the w console command reports network, address and RSSI.

One note, not a lecture: viktor14 is now a string literal in esp32_gateway.ino, so it goes into the repo the moment you commit. Fine for a hotspot key; just be aware if this repo ends up shared for the summer school.

problem: if i try to power the frdm board from 9V package, it will not power up

Definitive answer, from UM12012 Rev 2.0 Table 7 - your board is fine, and the schema is wrong. The FRDM-MCXA153 cannot be powered from J3-16 as shipped:

J3-16 P5-9V_VIN (5-9 V) -> J22 (1x3-pin footprint for a 5 V regulator module, NOT POPULATED) -> P5V_HDR_IN -> "third power source option (disabled by default)" for SYS_5V0.

Two independent breaks. The manual states it outright: "By default, the option to produce the SYS_5V0 supply from the P5V_HDR_IN supply is disabled." J3-16 feeds an empty footprint, so 9 V there goes nowhere.

The "5.0-9.0 V, board spec" line in FULL_SCHEMA.md:631 is the spec of a regulator that isn't fitted.

Two ways forward:
A - USB power bank into J15. Zero modification, and it keeps the MCU-Link powered so you still have VCOM.
B - regulate 9 V to 5 V yourself, into J3-10 (SYS_5V0), ground on J3-12 or J3-14. That's the rail both USB inputs land on.

Do not have USB and the pack connected at once on option B until you've checked how the three sources are OR'd onto SYS_5V0 - back-feeding a live VBUS path is how boards die.

Your four consoles agree on one thing: the MCX is doing nothing at all - not polling I2C, not writing to either Arduino, not printing. Every other symptom follows from that. queued 511 is the giveaway: the ESP32's outbound queue is full (max 512) with your keypresses, because nobody is collecting them.

That's my bug, and it's specific. I put imu_wake() - a blocking I2C transaction - before the startup banner. The SDK's I2C_RETRY_TIMES defaults to 0, which its own header documents as "keep waiting until the flag is assert/deassert": an unbounded wait, not a timeout. The bus has no pull-ups of its own, so with the IMU module absent or a bus wire off, SCL/SDA sit low and LPI2C_MasterTransferBlocking() never returns. The board hangs before printing a single character, which looks exactly like "never flashed".

Two fixes, both in:
1. Bounded I2C waits - -DI2C_RETRY_TIMES=100000 in CMakeLists.txt. I verified it actually reaches fsl_lpi2c.c, not just my own files.
2. The banner prints before any I2C, and the IMU wake now reports instead of blocking.

Reflash just the FRDM. Then the MCX console splits the remaining problem: banner + "IMU: NO ANSWER" means it was the hang; still nothing at all means USB must be in J15, not J8.

Good - the MCX is alive now. But one of your two symptoms was my diagnostic lying to you, and the other is real.

[act] VCU NEVER HEARD was expected, not a fault. The VCU only sends D, lines to ACT while something is actually driving - drive_service() returns immediately when not armed. With no browser driving, ACT correctly hears nothing, and my message called that a broken wire. PERC had a keep-alive (the horn line); ACT had none.

[perc] VCU silent is a genuine signal. PERC was getting H,0 every second in what you flashed, so that link really isn't delivering.

Fixed by giving both nodes the same treatment - a 1 Hz V,<uptime> heartbeat to both Arduinos, always. It carries the VCU's uptime so a board that silently reset is obvious, and it deliberately does not refresh ACT's 300 ms motor timeout.

I also had to fix two things my retry limit introduced. Your core runs at 12 MHz, so 100000 retries meant tens of milliseconds per failed transfer - with the gateway polled at 50 Hz, a dead I2C bus would have starved the drive loop. Now I2C_RETRY_TIMES=10000, the gateway backs off to 2 Hz while offline, and telemetry is skipped rather than failing slowly.

Build note: after a CMakeLists.txt change, use cmake --build --preset debug. Bare ninja tries to re-run CMake without the preset's environment and fails.

Noted - wiring per schema. That makes the loopback the decisive test, since it takes the wiring out of the picture entirely.

All nine pins are muxed at ALT2 and the clocks are attached - the code is right, so the fault is either the ALT value itself (the docs admit LPUART1's was "established by triangulation", never verified) or the wiring. Nothing currently distinguishes those. Built the tool that does.

The decisive test: loop1 / loop2. One jumper from the MCX's own TX to its own RX. No Arduino, no loom, no divider. If loop1 passes and loop2 fails, the ALT value in pin_mux.c is wrong and no wiring change would ever have fixed it.

Also new on the MCX console:
- mark1 / mark2 - transmits 0x55 for 5 s so a multimeter settles on the TX pin: ~1.8 V sending, 3.3 V idle, 0 V not muxed.
- raw1 / raw2 - every byte, in hex, bypassing line assembly. LINK_PollLine silently discards anything that never terminates, so a channel receiving garbage currently looks identical to one receiving nothing.

New sketch: link_debug.ino - same sketch for either Arduino, and it parses nothing. Every byte on D4 printed as hex. j = jumper test (proves that Arduino alone), e = echo mode (mirrors bytes back so tx1 tests both wires in one round trip).

Order: j on the Arduino, loop1/loop2 on the MCX, then e + tx1, then t. Steps 1 and 2 each involve one board and no cable.
what should i enter in consoles?

Step 4 - both consoles, everything wired. On PERC: e. Then on the MCX: tx1.

Steps 1-3 each test one board with no cable attached. Run them in order and stop at the first failure.

A hard fault is a different class of problem. Stack is only 2 KB (0x800), and the deepest chain (console_service -> drive_try_command -> test_link = 608 B of frames, plus PRINTF/sscanf internals) runs close to it.

Two changes:

1. Stack 2 KB -> 4 KB via --defsym=__stack_size__=0x1000. 24 KB SRAM, 7 KB used - the extra 2 KB is free.

2. A hard fault handler that talks. The SDK's is b . - an infinite loop, which is exactly the instruction your debugger stopped on. Mine prints PC, LR, PSR, R0-R3, HFSR and CFSR, decodes the fault bits by name, picks MSP vs PSP correctly from EXC_RETURN, and flags a stack overflow explicitly. Feed the PC to arm-none-eabi-addr2line and you get the exact source line.

Your ports, since it matters: COM3 = MCU-Link VCom (NXP), the FRDM - loop1, mark1, diag go here. COM4 = CP210x, the ESP32. There's no CH340 port, so neither Arduino is plugged into USB right now.

Then "no response to loop1" is itself the finding - and it fits everything else.

loop1 prints its header immediately, before any test runs. If you got nothing, the console isn't running code at all. Combined with the debugger landing in HardFault_Handler: the board faults, halts, and the console is dead - so every command produces nothing, the ESP32 sees reads 0, and both Arduinos hear silence. The hard fault is the root cause; everything else you've been chasing is downstream of it.

Your 3.3 V reading is good news: that's a correctly-muxed UART TX sitting idle. A pin not muxed to the LPUART would read 0 V or float. So the mux is fine - the firmware just isn't running.

Found it. The fault handler paid for itself immediately:

PC = GPIO_PinInit (fsl_gpio.c:216) - faulted writing PDDR
BFAR = 0x40103054 = GPIO1_BASE + 0x54
PRECISERR = bus error, peripheral not accessible

GPIO_PinInit(GPIO1, 7U, ...) - SW3 on P1_7 - was writing to a GPIO block still held in reset.

It's an SDK naming mismatch. fsl_gpio.c releases the GPIO reset only under #if defined(GPIO_RSTS), but MCXA153 defines it as GPIO_RSTS_N. The names don't match, so GPIO_RESETS_ARRAY is never defined and the reset release is compiled out entirely. GPIO_PinInit looks like it handles this - it does enable the clock - but on this part it silently doesn't release the reset.

pin_mux.c releases PORT1 and PORT3, which are different modules. GPIO3 got away with it because the board's red-LED init already released it - that's why only SW3 on P1_7 ever tripped it, and why the symptom presented as "the links don't work". It faults in test_extra_pins_init(), which runs before the banner, so the board died silently with the TX pins left idle at 3.3 V - exactly the multimeter reading you got.

Fixed by ungating and un-resetting GPIO1 and GPIO3 explicitly before use.

None of the link debugging was wrong, it was just unreachable - the board never got to main()'s loop.

[screenshots: [diag] GW DOWN 0 ok / 623 fail | PERC SILENT | ACT 123 ms | WEB silent; [gw] reads 0 (+0) writes 0 queued 511 dropped 0 ws 1]

i2c
-- I2C scan on LPI2C0 (P3_27 SCL / P3_28 SDA)
   nothing answered.

Nothing on the bus at all - not the ESP32, not the IMU. That's the classic no-pull-ups signature, and it's why the gateway has never worked.

Measure this first: with everything powered, probe against GND on the mikroBUS socket. J6 SCL (P3_27) and J6 SDA (P3_28) should both read 3.3 V. An idle I2C bus sits high on both lines. If they aren't at 3.3 V, no device can ever ACK and every transaction fails exactly as you're seeing - 623 times.

Then check the MPU6050 is actually connected, because on this design its on-board 2.2k are the only pull-ups on the entire bus: VCC to J3-8 (3.3 V, not 5 V), GND to star point, SDA to J6 SDA, SCL to J6 SCL. The ESP32 shares those same two wires.

If the IMU is missing or dead, you don't need it to drive - but you cannot run without pull-ups. Fit 4.7k (or 2.2k) from SCL and SDA to 3V3. Pull up to 3.3 V, never 5 V.
p3_28 and p3_27 are from J5. verify this

Checked against UM12012 Rev 2.0, Figure 12 - they're on J6. J5 is the SPI side.

J5 (SPI): AN=P3_30, RST=P3_1, CS=P1_3, SCK=P1_1, MISO=P1_2, MOSI=P1_0, +3V3=VDD_BOARD, GND.
J6 (I2C/UART): PWM=P3_12, INT=P2_5, RX=P3_14, TX=P3_15, SCL=P3_27, SDA=P3_28, +5V=SYS_5V0, GND.

That's the standard mikroBUS layout too. Your FULL_SCHEMA.md has it right as J6.

But don't count pins at all - read the silkscreen. The board prints the mikroBUS signal names beside the socket, so find the pins literally marked SCL and SDA.

One useful cross-check: P3_15 and P3_14 also appear on J6 as TX/RX - the same signals as PERC's link on J2-2/J2-4. If PERC is wired to the mikroBUS TX/RX by mistake, it would look exactly like the silent PERC link you have.
